boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Santa Rosa Island record (October 9, 1861) in Operations of the Gulf Blockading Squadron [October 1861]. The Pensacola harbor defences and the later reconnaissances on the island are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives the island garrison about 600 and the Confederate detachments about 1,200; the live field reads US 0 and CS 1,200. Brown estimated the landing force at 1,200 or 1,500 and says his officers' almost unanimous estimate was 1,500, later citing a Confederate acknowledgment of 1,500; he says less than 200 regulars and some 50 volunteers pursued five times their number. Anderson lists battalions of 350, 400 and 260 and an independent company of 53, with an artillery company not counted.
claims.rationale: Anderson's battalion figures sum to 1,063 before the uncounted artillery company; the CWSAC 1,200 is not traced to a return, and no inspected passage gives the island garrison's strength. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live US zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General Richard H. Anderson and Colonel Harvey Brown; the live page gives Anderson as Major General. Brown sent Vogdes and Arnold out from the fort and ordered Wilson to attack; Vogdes was captured before a shot was fired and Arnold succeeded to the command. Brown's October 12 letter says the volunteer regiment did not behave well. Anderson directed the columns and the withdrawal.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; NPS's statement that Brown sallied is not adopted over Brown's own account, the live rank is not adopted, and there is no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and the live field read 154 (US 67; CS 87). Brown's three accounts differ: on October 9, regulars 5 killed, about 15 wounded and 8 missing and volunteers 7, 8 or 9 and 10; on October 11, regulars 4, 20 and 8 and volunteers 10, 9 and a figure read 'IG'; on October 17, 4 and 9 killed, 20 and 7 wounded, 10 and 11 missing. He counts 14 enemy killed, 7 wounded and 27 prisoners in hand, quotes a Pensacola paper's 21 killed, 38 wounded and 22 prisoners, and a Confederate paper's 175. Anderson reports 18 killed, 39 wounded and 30 prisoners, estimates the Union loss at 50 or 60 killed and 100 wounded, and took 20 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Anderson's categories sum to 87, the CWSAC Confederate figure; that equality is not independent confirmation.

open_questions: Tower's, Arnold's, Wilson's and the other Union subordinate reports, Bragg's No. 14 reports, the Confederate battalion reports, Brown's table of distances (read, not cited), returns and maps remain deferred. No nineteenth-century history covering the action was selected.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Harvey Brown's October 9, 11, 12 and 17, 1861 reports are one family of interested Union accounts. R. H. Anderson's October 23, 1861 report is an interested Confederate account. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
